correctness.rationale: Root status: recomputed Tits q = -4,-5,-9,-11,-16,-4 for L; five vectors satisfy fundamental inequalities c1=2a-3b<=0,c2=2b-3a<=0; (2,4)=(-8,+2) reflects by s2 to (2,2) with q preserved, so all six are imaginary roots. DRAFT describes (2,4) correctly as non-fundamental Weyl-equivalent; s1 JSON label 'imag-fund' for (2,4) is loose but its stored path [(2,4),(2,2)] makes the route explicit. Schur-ness: independently recomputed dim End=1 for all six stored brick triples with fresh GF(2) nullspace code (6/6 OK). Upper-semicontinuity inference (one brick => general brick => Schur root => trivial Derksen-Weyman decomposition) is the standard theorem and is applied correctly. (2,2) census: fresh independent brute-force orbit enumeration gives 148 classes with masses summing to 4096, matching stored census; End distribution sums to 148 with 70 bricks; indecomposable count 98 via exhaustive idempotent search in End (sound: decomposable iff End has nontrivial idempotent). Dim-2 split by all-nonzero-invertible test gives 21 dual-number (absolutely indecomposable) + 7 F4 (not), hence A=70+21=91. (2,3) census: stored 402 classes with masses summing to 262144 exactly and orbit spectrum {1:1,21:7,42:14,84:7,126:28,252:91,504:43,1008:211}; all orbit sizes divide 1008; combined left/right action tables verified against naive H*M*Ginv matrices on 20 random trials; End distribution sums to 402 with 183 bricks; idempotent test gives 204 indecomposables = 183 End-1 + 21 End-2, spot-rechecked on 15 random classes with independent code (15/15 match); field-vs-local test gives 21 local + 0 F4, hence A=183+21=204. Stale s6_abs22.json reports nabs=77 via a characteristic-2-degenerate trace-radical computation and is superseded by the correct s6b invertibility split used in the DRAFT; not a headline defect but noted. No Kac q=2 values claimed above (2,3); limitations stated honestly.

originality.rationale: Substantive gap checked live, not by timestamp alone. Nearest priors state methods/existence only: Derksen-Weyman gives the general ext-vanishing canonical-decomposition algorithm; Schofield gives the general Schur/ext-orthogonality criterion; Kac gives the root-system existence criterion (real/imaginary) which underdetermines Schur-ness, summands, and q=2 counts; Weist (arXiv:0901.1780) proves existence of indecomposable tree modules for Kronecker quivers (coprime vectors glued, then factors for arbitrary roots), not per-vector Schur verdicts, summands, explicit F2 bricks, or Kac evaluations; QuiverTools (arXiv:2506.19432) ships the general tool (subdimension vectors, canonical decomposition, stability), not this evaluated 3-Kronecker table; Schiffmann survey (arXiv:1802.09760) covers Kac-polynomial theory/positivity with no small-vector q=2 table for this quiver; live arXiv search for 'Kronecker quiver Schur root canonical decomposition' returns no results and 'Kronecker+Schur' hits are symmetric-group coefficients (different usage). No source publishes Schur verdicts, these six brick matrices, trivial decompositions, or A(2,2)(2)=91 / A(2,3)(2)=204. Internal prior scan likewise disjoint (symmetric-group Kronecker, 5-vertex mutation census, etc.).

value.rationale: Headline is an exact invariant of a natural motivated object, not a textbook/parameter/gain/enumeration artifact. The 3-arrow Kronecker quiver is the minimal wild quiver past the tame 2-Kronecker threshold with pre-existing demand (Gabriel/Kac/Schofield/Derksen-Weyman, counting programs); Schur-ness, canonical summands, explicit bricks, and Kac q=2 counts were motivated before computation, are not known or mechanically implied by root lists/Euler form/primitives, and a future worker can need the precise datum (91 and 204 with witnesses, plus 6/6 Schur certificates). Narrowness (two exact counts, six bricks) does not disqualify under the exact-invariant clause. The dropped 'nontrivial summand' clause is disclosed; the delivered fallback Schur/brick/exact-count table is independently retrievable.
